chib-015.title: The Rockland eruption at Lassen
chib-015.text: More than 130 km³ of rhyolite magma erupted violently from the Lassen area of California, with huge pyroclastic flows and an ash plume tens of kilometres high. Recent studies put the Rockland ash at up to 326.7 km³, over twice the Mazama ash, so the Rockland eruption could be the most voluminous eruption in the Cascade Volcanic Arc. From 600,000 to 400,000 years ago, eruptions then built the large conical stratovolcano Mount Tehama. Another source rounds the comparison with Mazama to nearly twice.
